title: Course 1 Integrated Cultivation Workflow Practical
criticalErrors: Deliberately falsifies, fabricates, or forces a cultivation, identity, inventory, or traceability record.
Bypasses an explicit hold, quarantine, restricted-entry, or other supplied access-control instruction.
Attempts protected equipment servicing, energized technical work, or repair outside the stated Technician I authority.
Knowingly continues an explicit unsafe condition after the supplied procedure requires stopping or escalation.
Causes avoidable unrecoverable plant or material identity loss by ignoring a detected identity discrepancy.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Consistently complete, accurate, independent and well controlled. Decisions are supported by the supplied procedure/evidence and open conditions are transferred clearly.

levels.label: Competent
levels.description: Meets the expected Course 1 performance standard with only minor non-critical omissions that do not compromise safety, identity, traceability or record integrity.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Partially meets the standard but needs correction, prompting, stronger evidence or more reliable execution before independent course-level performance is demonstrated.

levels.label: Insufficient
levels.description: Does not yet demonstrate the required performance or leaves important controls, records, identity, authorization or handoff elements unresolved.

Safety, PPE and stop-work judgment.strong: Identifies seeded hazards and restrictions, uses supplied PPE/HazCom information correctly, preserves stop-work boundaries and escalates without unauthorized repair or release.
Safety, PPE and stop-work judgment.competent: Recognizes and controls the material hazards within role authority, stops or escalates when required, and avoids unsafe workarounds.
Safety, PPE and stop-work judgment.developing: Recognizes many hazards but misses or delays a non-critical control, needs prompting, or incompletely explains the authority boundary.
Safety, PPE and stop-work judgment.insufficient: Normalizes a material hazard, bypasses a required control, or cannot reliably distinguish routine work from stop/escalate conditions.

Sanitation and biosecurity.strong: Maintains clean-to-dirty movement logic, distinguishes sanitation from plant-health and worker-entry controls, and verifies product/process conditions before proceeding.
Sanitation and biosecurity.competent: Executes the supplied sanitation and movement controls correctly and preserves active restrictions.
Sanitation and biosecurity.developing: Completes most steps but misses a verification, sequence detail, or contamination pathway without creating a critical breach.
Sanitation and biosecurity.insufficient: Cannot reliably maintain movement/status controls or treats incompatible restrictions as interchangeable.

SOP and work-order execution.strong: Verifies current revision, task identity, scope, acceptance criteria and exceptions; identifies conflicts and transfers decisions cleanly without inventing authority.
SOP and work-order execution.competent: Works from the supplied controlled instruction and follows required stop, exception and escalation points.
SOP and work-order execution.developing: Follows the main sequence but needs help identifying a revision/scope/acceptance or exception boundary.
SOP and work-order execution.insufficient: Proceeds from an uncontrolled, conflicting or incomplete instruction without appropriate stop/escalation.

Identity and traceability.strong: Preserves physical and record identity through every movement, split/merge or handoff and blocks discrepant movement until resolution.
Identity and traceability.competent: Correctly verifies and records the required identifiers, movement context and destination/source relationships.
Identity and traceability.developing: Preserves core identity but misses a non-critical event/context field or needs prompting during reconciliation.
Identity and traceability.insufficient: Cannot reliably link physical material to the controlled record or attempts to force a mismatch to balance.

Inventory and discrepancy reasoning.strong: Separates confirmed from unresolved facts, preserves evidence and builds a defensible discrepancy/disposition trail without unsupported conclusions.
Inventory and discrepancy reasoning.competent: Detects, records and escalates discrepancies while preserving the actual physical and recorded state.
Inventory and discrepancy reasoning.developing: Finds the discrepancy but incompletely documents context, evidence or next ownership.
Inventory and discrepancy reasoning.insufficient: Forces reconciliation, obscures the mismatch or cannot identify what remains unknown.

Equipment readiness and operator-care bo.strong: Completes all permitted external readiness checks, identifies recurrence and operational impact, and escalates without unsupported diagnosis or protected servicing.
Equipment readiness and operator-care bo.competent: Performs the supplied operator checks and stays within the stated operator-care boundary.
Equipment readiness and operator-care bo.developing: Completes most checks but needs prompting on recurrence, documentation or the servicing boundary.
Equipment readiness and operator-care bo.insufficient: Attempts or recommends unauthorized servicing or cannot produce a usable equipment-status record.

Data integrity and documentation.strong: Produces contemporaneous, attributable, context-rich records; corrections preserve original history and missing information remains visibly missing.
Data integrity and documentation.competent: Creates reconstructable records and uses the supplied correction/late-entry process correctly.
Data integrity and documentation.developing: Records the core facts but misses context, timing, attribution or correction detail that requires remediation.
Data integrity and documentation.insufficient: Backfills, silently overwrites, guesses missing data or produces records that cannot be reliably reconstructed.

Shift handoff and communication.strong: Prioritizes safety/status, completed work, open deviations, ownership and time-sensitive next actions with two-way confirmation and source cross-checking.
Shift handoff and communication.competent: Communicates the required open/closed state and next ownership clearly enough for the incoming worker to act safely.
Shift handoff and communication.developing: Transfers most information but leaves a non-critical ambiguity, weak priority, or incomplete read-back.
Shift handoff and communication.insufficient: Omits material open conditions, presents hypotheses as facts, or fails to identify ownership/next action.

learnerWorkflow.overview: Apply Course 1 as one connected cultivation workflow while conditions change during a simulated shift. Learners must preserve safety, identity, traceability, authorization boundaries, record integrity, and handoff quality as new information appears.
learnerWorkflow.academicUse: The practical framework is public academic course content. It may be studied without authentication and used for simulation, supervised-lab, or workplace-equivalent learning and evaluation. Personal assessor results remain private learner records.
preparationSteps: Complete the Course 1 lessons, workbook activities, and low-stakes practice before attempting an evaluated practical.
Review the six Course 1 Field References and know which one applies to hazards, biosecurity, controlled work, traceability, equipment, and records/handoff.
Practice producing all seven required evidence outputs using the Course 1 workbook templates without inventing missing facts.
Be ready to explain when work must stop, what can proceed within Technician I authority, and what must be escalated to another role.
Expect conditions to change during the simulated shift and reassess earlier decisions when new status, identity, sanitation, equipment, or record information appears.

stages.title: 1. Pre-task review
stages.summary: Recognize hazards, access restrictions, work-order limits, identity risks, PPE needs, and operator authority before work begins.

stages.title: 2. Status and sanitation change
stages.summary: Reassess work when one restriction changes but another remains active, and verify exact sanitation-product authorization before substitution.

stages.title: 3. Recurring equipment fault
stages.summary: Stay inside the operator-care boundary, record the fault timeline, and escalate repeated unresolved conditions without unsupported diagnosis.

stages.title: 4. Record integrity
stages.summary: Correct records while preserving original history and distinguish observation time from later entry time without backdating.

stages.title: 5. Closed-loop handoff
stages.summary: Transfer unresolved holds, identity discrepancies, equipment status, sanitation status, and next actions using two-way read-back and source cross-checking.

supportResources: Course 1 remediation matrix and instructor coaching when assigned
learnerWorkflow.boundary: This is Course 1 practical learning and performance evidence. It is separate from the Technician I credential examination and does not by itself issue a professional credential.
